name: Giant Shrike
body:
Giant Shrike
CR 6

This fierce-looking bird’s ebon feathers gleam majestically, streaked with patterns of gray and brown. Its golden beak is tipped with white.

XP 2,400
N Large animal
Init +5; Senses low-light vision; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 15, flat-footed 13 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +4 natural, –1 size)
hp 75 (10 HD; 10d8+30)
Fort +10, Ref +12, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., fly 70 ft. (average)
Melee 2 talons +13 (1d6+5 plus grab), bite +12 (1d8+5)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks impale

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 20, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 9
Base Atk +7; CMB +13 (+21 grapple); CMD 28 (30 vs. grapple)
Feats Flyby Attack, Greater Grapple, Improved Grapple, Weapon Focus (talon), Wingover
Skills Acrobatics +8 Fly +16, Stealth +8

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Impale (Ex)

As a free action at the end of a movement while a giant shrike has a creature grappled and is adjacent to a jagged rock, tree, weathervane, or other similarly spiky protrusion, it can impale the grappled creature on it. The grappled creature takes 2d8+10 points of piercing damage (DC 20 Reflex half) and is no longer grappled; however, a creature failing its saving throw is entangled and unable to move. Each round at the beginning of its turn, an impaled creature takes an additional 1d8+5 points of piercing damage. It can end the entangled condition as a move action with a DC 16 Strength or Escape Artist check, taking an additional 1d8+5 points of piercing damage regardless of whether the check succeeds. If the shrike has impaled the creature on a high place, a creature that escapes impalement is considered to be climbing, with a DC determined by the nature of the place where they were impaled (GM’s discretion).

Vicious Snatcher (Ex)

A giant shrike that grapples a target while using its Flyby Attack feat does not gain the grappled condition and can move and carry along with it a Medium or smaller grappled creature without needing to make additional checks until the beginning of its next turn.

ECOLOGY

Environment cool areas with natural spikes, such as jagged mountain peaks or thorny forests
Organization solitary, watch (2-6), or flock (12-24)
Treasure none

Shrikes are passerine birds known for their habit of catching other birds and small animals and impaling the uneaten portions of their bodies on thorns. A typical shrike’s beak is hooked, like a bird of prey. When on the hunt, a winged shadow falls below this raptor as it stoops on its prey with a wingspan the length of four horses.
